Plug Power Emerges from Insolvency, Resumes Renewable Energy Operations in U.S.

NEW YORK, June 26 — Plug Power Inc, a key supplier in the United States renewable energy sector, has resumed operations after concluding a closely watched insolvency process that disrupted its business in recent weeks, company officials confirmed Wednesday.

The Latham, New York-based firm, best known for its hydrogen fuel cell technology, entered insolvency proceedings earlier this year following mounting losses and liquidity concerns, forcing a temporary halt to several of its manufacturing and deployment projects across multiple states.

On Monday, the company announced that it had completed a court-supervised restructuring process, with its primary operations returning to full capacity. The resolution included a sale of select assets to a consortium led by Blue Ridge Capital Partners and a refinancing package supported by existing creditors.

“We are grateful for the support of our employees, partners and stakeholders during this challenging period,” said Joseph Daniels, Interim CEO of Plug Power Inc, in a statement. “With the completion of our restructuring, Plug Power is positioned to continue its mission of accelerating the transition to clean energy.”

Plug Power employs more than 1,200 people nationwide, with major facilities in New York, Ohio, and Texas. The insolvency had led to the temporary furlough of approximately 400 workers and the suspension of deliveries to several large-scale commercial and municipal customers.

Local officials in Latham expressed relief at the company’s return. “Plug Power is an important part of our community and our economy,” said Albany County Executive Lisa Rodriguez. “We’re hopeful that this marks a new chapter for the company and its workforce.”

Industry analysts said the case underscores ongoing challenges facing renewable energy firms as they manage high upfront capital costs and navigate shifting federal incentives. “Plug Power’s insolvency was a wake-up call,” said Priya Menon, senior analyst at the Clean Energy Institute. “It shows the sector’s vulnerability to market volatility and financing constraints, even as demand for green technologies grows.”

The North American Renewable Energy Association welcomed the resumption of Plug Power’s operations, highlighting the firm's role in advancing hydrogen infrastructure. “We’re encouraged to see Plug Power emerge from this process and resume its critical work,” the association said in a statement.

Plug Power said it would prioritize re-hiring furloughed staff and restoring delayed projects, including new fuel cell installations for logistics and municipal fleets. Company officials indicated that further details on long-term strategy and investment plans are expected in the coming weeks.

Shares in Plug Power, which had been suspended from trading during the proceedings, are scheduled to resume on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday.
